newsitem.title: MEXICO: Spain's Juan Marse wins Mexico literary prize.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Juan Marse wins Mexico literary prize.

text.p: Spanish novelist Juan Marse has won Mexico's prestigious "Juan Rulfo" prize for literature, it was announced on Monday.
Marse will receive the prize of $100,000 during the 12th edition of the International Book Fair (FIL), to be held from Nov. 29 to Dec. 7 in Guadalajara, Mexico's second largest city.
The prize is awarded annually to writers from Latin America, the Caribbean or the Iberian peninsula, and is open to those who publish in English, French or Portuguese, in addition to Spanish.
A statement from the FIL organisers said the jury for the prize had decided "unanimously" to award the prize to Marse.
Marse, born in 1933, is probably best-known to English speakers for "The Bilingual Lover," the 1993 film version of his novel "El Amante Bilingue."
